title: CALCE battery cycling data: CS2 cells
publisher: Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering, U. Maryland
citation: He, W., Williard, N., Osterman, M., Pecht, M. Prognostics of lithium-ion batteries based on Dempster-Shafer theory and the Bayesian Monte Carlo method. Journal of Power Sources 196(23), 10314-10321 (2011). Also cited by CALCE for CS2: Xing et al., Microelectronics Reliability 53(6), 811-820 (2013); Williard et al., Int. J. Prognostics and Health Management 4, 1-7 (2013).
attribution: Data: CALCE Battery Research Group, University of Maryland (calce.umd.edu/battery-data), CS2 cells; cite He, Williard, Osterman and Pecht, J. Power Sources 196 (2011) 10314-10321, as CALCE asks. Per-cycle values computed by Lemonergy (battery-data).
publication_basis: CALCE publishes the data openly and asks that its articles be cited, but states no licence, so the raw files are not redistributed here. What is published are per-cycle values Lemonergy computed from them (facts about each cycle), with the citation CALCE asks for. Published on the owner's instruction of 30 October 2026; withdrawn if CALCE asks.

batches.CS2: 15 CS2 cells (CS2_3 to CS2_38); CALCE's page gives each cell's test conditions

method: Each cell's session files (Arbin .xlsx or CADEX .txt) merged with battery-data tools/convert_calce_cs2.py and its cycles computed with tools/cyclers.py (cycle = one charge followed by one discharge; capacity integrated from current) at battery-data 5d881c9: the cycle_summary rows of the CALCE import. Values are rounded as printed: Ah and volts to 4 decimals, efficiency to 5, seconds to 0.1.
caveats: CS2_3 (12-18 October 2012) and CS2_25 (4-5 March 2013) each hold two different recordings of the same period; the session that starts first is kept and the overlapping rows of the other dropped. CALCE was asked on 30 October 2026 which is correct.
CS2_8 and CS2_21 were tested on a CADEX tester whose files carry no clock: their sessions are joined end to end, so the gaps between sessions are unknown and start times are not calendar times.
CS2_3 and CS2_9 use stepped discharge currents; the tester counts cycles by its own schedule (863 and 204), battery-data by charge-discharge pairs (1,361 and 1,181).
Rests, short top-ups and other partial cycles are rows too; a full discharge is one that reaches the 2.7 V cut-off (v_min at or below 2.75 V).

CS2_8 cycle 574 and CS2_21 cycle 425 each hold two charges and one discharge, because the CADEX recording has no discharge between the two charges; their charge_ah and coulombic_efficiency are not a normal cycle's (see exceptions).

coulombic_efficiency.meaning: discharge_ah / charge_ah (meaningless when charge_ah is near zero)

start_test_time_s.meaning: start of the cycle on the cell's merged time axis

exceptions.reason: The CADEX recording holds a full charge to 4.2 V, then about a minute with no current recorded while the voltage falls to 3.68 V, then a second charge, before one discharge: the cycle derived from current holds two charges, so its charge is about twice a normal cycle's and its coulombic efficiency about 0.5. Kept as recorded.
